title: Explicit rational witness for one-variable signed inequalities
statement:
Let $I$ be a finite set and let $a_i,b_i\in\mathbf Q$ for every $i\in I$ [def-weil-field]. Put $I_0=\{i:a_i=0\}$, $I_+=\{i:a_i>0\}$ and $I_-=\{i:a_i<0\}$. Suppose that $b_h\ge0$ for $h\in I_0$, $b_i\ge0$ for $i\in I_+$, and $a_i b_j-a_j b_i\ge0$ for every $(i,j)\in I_+\times I_-$. Then
$$B=\{0\}\cup\{b_j/a_j:j\in I_-\}\subseteq\mathbf Q$$
is finite and nonempty, and has a largest member $T\in\mathbf Q$. This member satisfies
$$T\ge0,\qquad T\ge b_j/a_j\ (j\in I_-),\qquad T\le b_i/a_i\ (i\in I_+),\qquad b_i-Ta_i\ge0\ (i\in I).$$
No nonemptiness of $I$, $I_+$ or $I_-$ is assumed; if $I_-=\varnothing$ then $T=0$.

proof.text: Since $I$ is finite, list its negative-sign indices as $j_1,\ldots,j_r$, allowing $r=0$. Their coefficients are nonzero, so put $c_k=b_{j_k}/a_{j_k}\in\mathbf Q$. Then $B=\{0,c_1,\ldots,c_r\}$ is finite and contains $0$. Define $t_0=0$ and $t_k=\max(t_{k-1},c_k)$, choosing the larger of the two rationals. By induction, $t_k\in\{0,c_1,\ldots,c_k\}$ and every member of that set is at most $t_k$: this holds at $k=0$, and replacing the previous largest value by the larger of it and $c_k$ preserves both assertions. Thus $T=t_r\in B$ is its largest member; in particular $T\ge0$ and $T\ge b_j/a_j$ for each $j\in I_-$.

source.place: Agent-written elementary proof of the extracted one-variable witness; ILO VIII Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103, is contextual only.

proof.text: Fix $i\in I_+$ and $j\in I_-$. Here $a_i(-a_j)>0$, and direct subtraction gives $$\frac{b_i}{a_i}-\frac{b_j}{a_j}=\frac{a_i b_j-a_j b_i}{a_i(-a_j)}\ge0.$$ The numerator is nonnegative by the pairwise hypothesis and the denominator is positive. Consequently $b_j/a_j\le b_i/a_i$ for every such pair. Also $0\le b_i/a_i$, since $b_i\ge0$ and $a_i>0$.

source.place: Agent-written elementary proof of the extracted one-variable witness; ILO VIII Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103, is contextual only.

proof.text: For any fixed $i\in I_+$, Step 2 shows that every member of $B$ is at most $b_i/a_i$: its members are $0$ or one of the negative-sign ratios. Because $T\in B$ by Step 1, it follows that $T\le b_i/a_i$. If $I_+$ is empty this assertion is vacuous; no positive-sign index was chosen globally.

source.place: Agent-written elementary proof of the extracted one-variable witness; ILO VIII Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103, is contextual only.

proof.text: For $i\in I_+$, the upper bound and $a_i>0$ give $Ta_i\le b_i$, hence $b_i-Ta_i\ge0$. For $j\in I_-$, multiplying $T\ge b_j/a_j$ by the negative number $a_j$ reverses the inequality and gives $Ta_j\le b_j$, hence $b_j-Ta_j\ge0$. For $h\in I_0$, $b_h-Ta_h=b_h\ge0$ by hypothesis. These three cases exhaust $I$. If $I_-=\varnothing$, the list in Step 1 is empty, $B=\{0\}$ and $T=t_0=0$. This includes $I=\varnothing$; all indexed inequalities are then vacuous.
